newsitem.title: USA: U.S. House votes to release data on Nazis.
newsitem.headline: U.S. House votes to release data on Nazis.

text.p: The House of Representatives on Tuesday called on the federal government to make public its records on Nazi war criminals, which have been kept secret since the end of the Second World War.
The non-binding resolution, which passed by voice vote, asks that the information be made available through the Freedom of Information Act, which allows individuals to request government records.

"With this resolution, the House will go on record in favour of full disclosure of war crimes files, so long as the release of this information does not harm our legitimate national security interests," Representative Carolyn Maloney, a New York Democrat who was a sponsor of the measure, said.
She said the Central Intelligence Agency objected to passage of a bill requiring release of the information.
"In passing this resolution, we honour the memory of those who died and the suffering of those who survived (the Holocaust)," she said.
